creator: itstundealao
title: Fact-or-hype test of MiroFish, an open-source multi-agent 'prediction' simulator, used to predict which of 5 video scripts performs best on Instagram

tools.name: MiroFish
tools.detail: Open-source GitHub repo (Chinese UI, switchable to English); tagline 'Predict Anything before it happens' / 'Upload Reports, Predict the Future'; run locally at localhost

tools.name: OpenAI API
tools.detail: Simulation consumes OpenAI credits ('hope this does not kill my OpenAI credits')

tools.name: Claude
tools.detail: Asked the same question as a baseline; picked Episode 14

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.detail: Terminal-style agent output: 'Transcribed all 5 videos locally with Whisper and combined them into one PDF'

claims: MiroFish spins up 'hundreds of AI people' who debate a question like social media users; site says up to million-scale agents
Creator fed transcripts of 5 recent videos; MiroFish picked the '/brag' video (Episode 17), which did get the most views (900,000 at time of recording)
Claude asked the same question picked Episode 14, 'pretty sure actually the worst performing one'
Verdict: FACT, but 'not sure until I test it on more cases'
Simulation 'is taking a while' and costs OpenAI credits
how_to_steps: Clone the MiroFish repo, add environment variables (OpenAI key), run it
Switch UI language from Chinese to English
Have Claude Code transcribe source videos with Whisper and compile into a PDF (one per page with titles)
Upload the PDF and ask 'Which video will perform the best on Instagram'
Pipeline stages: Graph Build -> Env Setup -> Simulation -> Report -> Interaction; wait for 'report generation is complete'
Read the 'Instagram Video Performance Prediction Report' and compare to real results
on_screen_only: Overlay 'Fact or Hype?' with FACT / HYPE checkboxes; FACT checked at the end

MiroFish landing: 'Predict Anything', 'The World's First Simple and Universal Open-Source Swarm Intelligence Engine', 'Join the waitlist', 'Upload Reports, Predict the Future... extracts every needed entity to auto-generate a parallel world with up to million-scale Agents... Let Agents rehearse the future, let decisions prevail'; badges 'Low Cost', 'Scalable'
Knowledge graph with Chinese node labels (e.g. 华中科技大学, 抖音/短视频平台, Reddit, 青年教师, 中国社会科学院)

Claude Code output: 'Done. Transcribed all 5 videos locally with Whisper and combined them into one PDF each on its own page with a short title. Episode 15: Claude Skill for Startup Pricing; Episode 17: The /brag Skill: Instant Launch Videos; Episode 16: Claude Code Builds a 3D Rocket Game; Episode 15: Caveman Skill Cuts Claude Token Usage; Episode 14: Connecting a WOOP Tracker to Claude Code'; later 'My pick: Episode 14 (WOOP heart rate tracker)... Runner-up would be Episode 16 (3D rocket/game build)'

MiroFish Report Agent: 'Based on the provided scripts, the video that is likely to perform the best on Instagram would be one that features Episode 17: The /brag Skill: Instant Launch Videos' and 'Key factors in video performance' sections
Localhost UI with tabs Graph Build / Simulation / Report Generation; Chinese agent posts/comments in the simulated feed

relevance.why: Interesting but a single-case anecdote; agent-swarm simulation is slow, costs API credits and is unproven as a product-decision tool for a time-poor founder.

implement_score.why: Do not adopt. If content prediction matters, a cheap alternative is asking Claude to score hooks against known patterns; revisit only if independent evaluations show MiroFish beats a baseline.

verify: MiroFish GitHub org/repo, license, maintenance status and actual agent count/cost per run
One correct pick out of five is weak evidence; any benchmark on real prediction accuracy?
Does the tool send your documents to third-party APIs?
